_comment: Multi-repo ADO daemon profile rooted on the NOVA_reviews store. Select with `CodeReviewDaemon --review nova`. The store (github.com/gautamb_microsoft/NOVA_reviews) is on GITHUB while every reviewed repo is on AZURE DEVOPS — that split is supported: Program.cs pins the store preparer's provider to 'github' and DeriveAdoOrgs harvests 'o365exchange' from EnabledRepos, so the host git runner carries an ADO credential for the submodule fetches. Verified against the store 2026-08-06: 5 submodules, all `shallow = true`, seeded on branch main with README.md, PRs/.gitkeep, KnowledgeBase/.gitkeep and KnowledgeBase/_toc.md. See ADO-ONBOARDING.md; this profile supersedes appsettings.astra.json, which named a store (AstraReview) that was never created.

Ado._comment: azure-devops-mcp public client id (see LmStreaming.Sample/AuthProviderGuide.md). MSAL.NET interactive (browser + loopback + PKCE), no secret. TenantId is pinned to the Microsoft corp tenant rather than 'common': o365exchange is backed by that tenant, and pinning stops MSAL from offering a personal MSA that can never see these repos. Sign in ONCE out-of-band into the shared TokenStoreDir below; the daemon has no `auth` subcommand and restores the sign-in at boot via OAuthTokenHydrator, refreshing through AcquireTokenSilent.

Auth._TokenStoreDir_comment: Shared with LmStreaming.Sample so a sign-in performed in the chat UI is the one the daemon rehydrates. Holds msal-ado.bin (ADO) and github.json (gautamb_microsoft, scopes repo + read:org — the credential that clones the NOVA_reviews store).

SandboxGateway._comment: WorkspaceBasePath is deliberately NOT set here. UseS2SReviewAgent makes one mandatory (Program.cs throws 'no workspace base path is configured'), but it is a property of the RUNNING GATEWAY, not of this profile, and the gateway exposes no endpoint that reads it back — api/v1/config, api/v1/info and api/v1/workspaces all 404, leaving only /health, api/v1/sandboxes and api/v1/marketplaces/preview. So the client SDK cannot discover it and this profile must not hardcode it. Supply it at launch through CRD_WORKSPACE_BASE_PATH, which Program.cs prefers over this key. AUTH_ENFORCE=false on this gateway, so CRD_SANDBOX_APP_KEY is not needed.

CodeReviewDaemon._LmStreamingBaseUrl_comment: ENFORCED AT STARTUP as of ReviewHostCollaborationPreflight — the daemon now probes GET api/conversations/{id}/agents/{agentId}/transcript at boot (gated on UseS2SReviewAgent) and REFUSES TO START when the host answers code=collaboration_unavailable, so this is no longer a comment you have to have read. Only that exact code fails; a timeout, an unreachable host or any other status passes, because none of those establishes the setting is off and a startup assertion that trips on a blip is worse than none. The probe needs no real conversation: code=unknown_thread is the healthy answer. Start the host with AgentCollaboration__Enabled=true, e.g. `AgentCollaboration__Enabled=true dotnet run --project samples/LmStreaming.Sample`. That setting is what makes the transcript route answer at all: with it off (the sample's shipped default) the route returns 404 collaboration_unavailable, and ReviewNotesArtifactBuilder writes the sub-agent's note as a ~750-byte stub whose whole body is 'The daemon could not read this transcript from the review host'. Observed on PRs 5501480 and 5501629 — the lead-reviewer note was full (the daemon holds that conversation itself) while all five delegate notes were stubs. Not retroactive: the hierarchy rows a collaboration-off host persisted carry no node record, so already-reviewed PRs stay stubbed. Only Enabled needs changing — MaxDelegationDepth 1 is exactly the one ordinary hop the host already allows with collaboration off, and TranscriptVisibility Ancestors already admits this reader, which names no viewer and is therefore treated as the conversation root.
CodeReviewDaemon._LmStreamingReviewMarketplace_comment: VERIFIED against this box's gateway: the alias is 'gb', not the 'gb-plugins' the achieveai/mcqdb/s2s profiles use (those were written for a different gateway). GET api/v1/marketplaces/preview?marketplaces=gb-plugins returns 400 'unknown marketplace alias(es)' with available=[local,superpowers,gb], which under RequireSkillSupport=true would stop the daemon at boot. 'gb' carries code-reviewer 1.19.0 (pr-review skill + 13 code-reviewer:* agents).
CodeReviewDaemon._Marketplaces_comment: Stated explicitly, and it must be: this key defaults to ['gb-plugins','superpowers'], and leaving it unstated is not the same as leaving it alone. Observed 2026-08-06 — with it absent, 43 consecutive runs reached the review call and died on 'Response status code does not indicate success: 400' from LmStreamingS2SClient, because the session provisioning asked this gateway for the gb-plugins alias it does not publish. The reviewed-repo checkout was fine; the runs failed at Reviewed, not ContextReady. Both aliases here are confirmed against api/v1/marketplaces/preview, which reports available=[local,superpowers,gb].
CodeReviewDaemon._EnableCommentPosting_comment: Collect-only. These are live, shared repos with active PRs, so flipping this to true immediately posts Revobot threads onto other people's work — leave it false until a collect-only run has been eyeballed in nova-review.db.
CodeReviewDaemon._EnabledRepos_comment: One entry per store submodule, as 'org/project/repo' — PrPollTargetBuilder reads the 3 segments positionally as OrgOrOwner/Project/RepoName, splitting on '/' only, so the space in 'O365 Core' is preserved rather than treated as a separator. All five pair with their store submodule: SubmoduleTargetsRepo now canonicalizes the legacy '{org}.visualstudio.com' host and its implicit DefaultCollection segment (Astra and MODISService are declared that way) and percent-decodes before comparing, so 'O365%20Core' in .gitmodules matches the 'O365 Core' written here. See CrossRepoCheckoutTests.SubmoduleTargetsRepo_pairs_every_url_spelling_of_the_same_repo, which pins each of those spellings.
CodeReviewDaemon._CrossRepoSiblings_comment: The other repos in the store, co-located beside whichever one is under review so a PR can be read against the code it actually talks to. DaemonReviewStageExecutor.AllowsCrossRepoCoLocation gates this on !IsForkPr && !IsTargetRepoPublic, which holds for every one of these internal ADO repos — but ONLY since the poller was taught to populate those two flags. Before that nothing wrote either, both defaulted true (fail closed), and this whole setting was inert: measured across 138 runs, 4 of the 5 store submodules were refused on every single one (416 'not on the allow-list' denials over 104 runs). If those denials ever come back, read the poll logs before touching this list — the cause is far more likely to be the trust signal than a wrong path here. Note what the signal actually depends on: ADO's PR-list payload does NOT carry repository.project.visibility at all (it serializes project as the shallow {id, name, state} reference), so AdoPrProvider resolves visibility from the org-scoped project API (GET {org}/_apis/projects/{project}) and caches it per project for the process. Grep for its Warning, 'Could not establish the target project's visibility' — that is the line that names the cause, and it fires only when both the payload and the project API failed. PrPollingService's Debug 'could not establish the confidentiality trust signal' says which half went unestablished. If instead you see an OperationPolicy denial on '/_apis/projects/', the project route fell out of ReviewScope.ApiProjectMetadataPath and the lookup is being egress-blocked. Each is written '{project}/{repo}' rather than as a bare name: an unqualified ADO sibling resolves under the REVIEWED repo's project, which is wrong the moment the store spans projects — reviewing WeveNova (O365 Core) would otherwise look for 'O365 Core/_git/Nova', which does not exist. The org is always the reviewed repo's (o365exchange), since a store's submodules are same-org by construction. Listing all five, including the repo under review, is harmless — the reviewed repo is unconditionally allow-listed anyway, so its entry is just a duplicate rule.
CodeReviewDaemon._ReviewedRepoSubmodules_comment: Intentionally absent: this is the allow-list for a REVIEWED repo's OWN nested submodules, not for the store's. None of the five checkouts carries a .gitmodules of its own today. Add URL repo-name segments here if that changes — it is an explicit allow-list, never a same-org wildcard.
CodeReviewDaemon._store_comment: The store repo, seeded and populated. It is a GitHub superproject whose submodules are ADO repos, so the store clone authenticates with github.json while each submodule fetch authenticates with the ADO token. Both URLs point at the same repo because the review store and the ReviewBot retention repo ARE one repo (ResolvedStoreUrl falls back from CrossRepoStoreUrl to ReviewBotRepoUrl).
CodeReviewDaemon._ReviewPoolHostRoot_comment: Deliberately unset — it would be inert. Program.cs derives poolLeaf from this key's final segment, but the S2S branch immediately overrides poolRoot to effectiveWorkspaceBase and switches the slot prefix to 'review-', discarding that leaf. With UseS2SReviewAgent=true the pool always lands directly under the gateway-supplied base, one mount per repo: {base}/review-{repo-slug}.
CodeReviewDaemon._ReviewPoolSize_comment: Concurrent reviews across the whole daemon, not per repo. Under the worktree pool a repo's slots share ONE store clone and one submodule clone — each slot adds two git worktrees (a notes worktree and the reviewed checkout), so the marginal disk cost of a slot is a working tree, not another copy of the object database. The cap is about how much review work runs at once, not about disk.
CodeReviewDaemon._KnowledgeModelId_comment: SPEND-NEUTRALITY PIN. This key was inert on the S2S path until S2SReviewAgentLoopFactory started forwarding modelId as the conversation's provider id; its previous value here was 'claude-opus-4.8', which the factory silently ignored, so the at-close extraction passes have in fact been running on gpt-5.6-terra. Pinned to the model actually in use so the plumbing fix changes no spend. Restoring 'claude-opus-4.8' is now a real, one-token config edit — and it will now take effect.
